analysis.title: TotalEnergies SE: Estimates and PT moving higher
key_insights: RBC raises its TotalEnergies (TTE) price target from €85 to €90 and keeps its Outperform rating after 3Q26 results and an updated commodity price deck.
3Q26 was helped by integration across upstream and downstream. Refining strength and strong gas trading results were features of the quarter, and RBC expects both to repeat in 4Q26.
Middle East exposure has fallen sharply. Affected production was about 15% of the total at 1Q26 results and is now under 5%, so the group-level earnings hit is minimal.
Management reinforced its distribution framework and is willing to top up payouts through year-end to reach the 40% payout ratio on CFFO, despite the pre-announced 4Q26 and 1Q27 buybacks.
RBC models a special dividend announced in 4Q26 (€0.2/sh, $507m) and paid in 1Q27, which brings the rolling 12-month payout ratio in line with guidance by 1Q27.
With gearing falling below 10%, RBC sees room for elevated distributions. It forecasts $9bn of buybacks in 2027 and $6.3bn in 2026.
Estimate changes come mostly from the new price deck of $91/bbl Brent in 2026 and $88/bbl in 2027, plus continued strength in refining margins.
RBC's 2026E adjusted EPS rises to $13.00 from $12.35 and 2027E to $12.52 from $11.47, while 2028E falls to $11.31 from $11.65.
Valuation: TTE trades at a slight premium to the sector on 2027E EV/DACF (5.4x vs a 4.7x peer average) with an in-line FCF yield of 10.6%, both on forward curve pricing.
The price target blends 50% SOTP (€87.6) and 50% normalised EV/DACF at 8.0x (€91.2). The weighted average is €89.4, rounded up to €90.
RBC's upside scenario is €115 (Brent at $100/bbl in 2027 and mid-cycle refining and chemicals earnings). Its downside scenario is €60 (Brent at $50/bbl and downstream earnings near 2008-09 levels).

RBC argues TTE is defensive. It was the only European major not to cut its dividend through the worst of the pandemic, and it is positioned as the 'growthy' European major with upstream projects delivering growth into the 2030s.
The RBC European and US integrated comp sheet rates TTE, BP, Repsol, Galp and Chevron Outperform. Aramco, Exxon, Shell, Eni, Equinor and OMV are Sector Perform.

earnings_insights: TTE 3Q26 reported results (already printed) showed refining strength and strong gas trading results. RBC expects both to repeat in 4Q26.
RBC estimate (adjusted, USD): 2026E EPS $13.00 vs previous $12.35, 2027E $12.52 vs $11.47, 2028E $11.31 vs $11.65. 2025A adjusted EPS was $6.89.
RBC estimate: 2026E operating CFPS $18.81 vs previous $17.83, 2027E $18.04 vs $17.06, 2028E $17.13 vs $17.55.
RBC estimate: DPS 2026E €3.80 vs previous €3.60. 2027E €3.82 and 2028E €4.04 are unchanged.
RBC quarterly net earnings in $m: 1Q26A 5,394, 2Q26A 6,027, 3Q26A 9,097, 4Q26E 8,403, giving 2026E adjusted net income of 28,921.
RBC estimate: 2026E adjusted net income rises 6.2% to $28,921m from $27,235m. 2027E rises 10.7% to $26,926m and 2028E falls 1.9% to $23,509m.
RBC estimate: Refining & Chemicals earnings are $9,932m in 2026E (up 6.2% vs old), $6,017m in 2027E and $3,849m in 2028E. Integrated LNG rises 11.0% in 2026E and 22.7% in 2027E.
RBC estimate: 4Q26 special dividend of €0.2/sh ($507m) paid in 1Q27. 2027 buybacks of $9bn and 2026 buybacks of $6.3bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: RBC's updated price deck is the main driver of the estimate increases for TTE.
RBC's 2027 deck supports 2027E EPS of $12.52 for TTE.
Forward curve pricing as of Oct 28, 2026, used for RBC's comp sheet valuation multiples.
Strip gas prices used in the comp sheet valuation.

risk_factors: Downside risk to the oil price.
High exposure to Africa, which remains exposed to civil unrest.
Risk from operations in Russia given the current environment.
Management may be more cautious than peers in bull markets.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict: production affected fell from about 15% of TTE's total at 1Q26 results to under 5% now, so the earnings impact at group level is minimal.
Russia: operations in the country are a stated risk to RBC's rating and price target.
Africa: high exposure to a region that remains exposed to civil unrest.
